purpose: Internal Meta_Kim decision data distilled from inspected reference material and Meta_Kim boundaries. Kim_Decision may be discovered through the dependency registry, but these patterns do not authorize invoking Kim_Decision or any other project as an execution dependency.

referenceOnly: Kim_Decision external/local reference discovered through META_KIM_DEP_ROOTS, sibling scan, installed skills, registry, or GitHub evidence
sourceBoundary.distillationRule: Absorb reusable decision concepts into Meta_Kim stage data; do not copy another project's workflow shape or make it a callable provider.

internalizedAs: required failures cannot be averaged away
explicit, implicit, contextual and negative cases
limitations: skill evaluation is not native Agent loading evidence

internalizedAs: outcome equivalence rather than one reference tool sequence
limitations: no upstream benchmark score is reused

internalizedAs: discover material extraction capability only when needed
preserve original source and extraction limitations
limitations: converter adapter remains optional and uninstalled
OCR or cloud conversion needs separate capability and authorization evidence

internalizedAs: concurrency and request start-rate are separate controls
only a controlled invocation surface can be paced
limitations: no second scheduler or persistent queue
no claim to control all host requests or fix global 429 responses
no pack resolver or second orchestrator

internalizedAs: stop when execution-relevant uncertainty is resolved
limitations: retired gsd-build/get-shit-done is migration provenance, not active dependency
no PROJECT.md or second requirements authority

internalizedAs: separate unresolved human choices from implementation details
limitations: LICENSE text verified; API NOASSERTION is not license content
no fixed plan approval ritual or deferred queue

internalizedAs: goal draft is a suggestion distinct from permission
limitations: read-only alignment and advisory goal_draft only
does not replace Meta requirements, scheduler or permission authority

stagePatterns.pattern: Bind the current user request and its acceptance criteria before selecting a route; keep framework maintenance acceptance separate.
useWhen: a model or route claims success
rejects: fixed framework roadmap as the user's goal
all tasks treated as industry or coding tasks
stagePatterns.verification: The requested task, Critical intent and run-scoped goal stay bound; changing the request or acceptance criteria invalidates prior outcome observations.

stagePatterns.pattern: Assess declared task outcomes with evidence, separately from structural checks, routing and native invocation.
useWhen: a deliverable is ready for review
a candidate route needs a small falsification test
an eval report is used as acceptance evidence
rejects: model score compensates for a required failure
a reference trajectory is required without a contract reason
cached or synthetic results called live acceptance
stagePatterns.verification: Run npm run meta:eval:governance; supplied observation assessment remains separate from authenticated execution and user acceptance.

stagePatterns.pattern: Discover suitable input and invocation capabilities only where the task needs them, preserving evidence and scheduling authority.
useWhen: controlled requests face resource constraints or rate limits
outputs: selected converter or explicit capability gap
rejects: timeout assumed to stop a side effect
local queue claimed to govern all host traffic
stagePatterns.verification: Require actual material fidelity or controlled-invocation evidence before activating a converter or limiter; method guidance alone does not establish runtime support.

stagePatterns.pattern: Lock the actual decision or artifact before expanding the frame.
useWhen: the task could branch into product, code, strategy, or governance work
rejects: asking questions that do not change execution
stagePatterns.verification: intentPacket explains what changes, for whom, how success is tested, and which unknowns block execution.

stagePatterns.pattern: Classify evidence by certainty and decision impact before it drives route selection.
rejects: external project claim without inspection status
stagePatterns.verification: Every material claim has source, confidence, and route/risk/acceptance impact.

stagePatterns.pattern: Map the subject from current state to target state through candidate paths before dispatch.
useWhen: minimal fix and shortest correct path differ
ten-x route may change the outcome
stagePatterns.verification: Selected path beats alternatives on goal fit, time to proof, risk, reversibility, automation potential, and verification strength.

stagePatterns.pattern: Define the smallest action that can change the decision before scaling execution.
useWhen: dependency/routing confidence is below execution threshold
product or strategy claim needs proof
stagePatterns.verification: The first action has input, action, output, pass signal, kill signal, and timebox.

stagePatterns.pattern: A stage reached is not a stage passed; review must decide pass, revise, kill, or return to evidence.
useWhen: workflow output exists but user goal may not be done
stagePatterns.verification: Review can reproduce evidence and closes or blocks every critical/high finding.

stagePatterns.pattern: Bind PR, issue, or release work to the highest-risk capability lane before choosing a learning or execution skill.
useWhen: user asks how to prioritize skill improvement
PR or issue evidence is being triaged
decisionRules: localized routing, stage feedback, or choice surface change -> multilingual QA
review finding, changelog, release note, or progress closure -> review closure discipline
hook, dispatch, state, validator, warning, or route progression change -> state-machine failure modeling
tie-break by failure cost: install/runtime breakage, wrong execution or repeated hook blocks, incomplete public closure, localized route failure
rejects: four skills treated as equal priority
skill advice without PR, issue, run, or review evidence
learning plan not tied to the next executable gate
stagePatterns.verification: Decision names one primary skill lane, at most one secondary lane, the evidence that forced it, and the gate where it will be used next.

stagePatterns.pattern: Cross-check decision claims against current state, counterevidence, and replayable commands before public closure.
useWhen: PR or issue state can change
public-ready or closure claim is about to be made
user challenges whether the decision is rigorous enough
minimumChecks: current-state recheck for PRs, issues, releases, versions, platform support, or external claims
source triangulation or explicit single-source limitation
claim-to-source mapping for every material recommendation
fresh verification command or artifact for local repository claims
stagePatterns.verification: An independent reviewer can replay the commands or source links and either reproduce the verdict or identify which contradiction changes the route.

stagePatterns.pattern: Resolve discoverable facts, replay concrete outcomes, preserve settled decision evidence, and feed the existing route and capability bindings; keep route decisions separate from action permission.
stagePatterns.verification: Behavior regressions and independent actual local task review; offline selection alone does not prove live tool invocation or model quality.
